gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-vend-sans: Conthrax's lowercase a gapes wide, and its capitals barely rise above it. Vend Sans, a plain sans drawn with a ruler's constant line, can go a size down since its lowercase fills the line anyway.
gen-dafont-crust-clean-fs-erode: Erode reads with a dignified, editorial hush, its stroke weight easing gently across a generous middle band. And Crust Clean, with nearly sealed rounds and a laser-etched line, makes Erode's open g and a feel generous.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-alexandria: Alexandria leaves its c terminals gaping, with short stems above and below the body. Alexandria reads clean and smooth paragraph after paragraph, while Disorder keeps its raw, chaotic glyphs well apart.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-amiko: Disorder lets curves meet stems with no swelling, like a marker. Where Disorder grabs attention with its big, loosely spaced lowercase, Amiko does the quieter job of reading well, its outward-pointing terminals keeping letters distinct.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-anek-gujarati: Anek Gujarati has a lowercase that rivals its capitals and a gaping c opening. And Disorder, its curves matching its stems in weight, wants a bigger size, while Anek Gujarati can drop down a notch.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-anek-gurmukhi: Flat, loud and shade-free: that is Disorder at first glance. Anek Gurmukhi supplies wide counters in every small letter and open-handed curves, giving the rough heading a clear-headed partner underneath.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-anek-latin: Rough, flat-lined and wild, Disorder runs one unswelling stroke around every curve, with its glyphs set well apart. Anek Latin keeps its letters held open, so reading moves along smoothly.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-anek-tamil: Blunt and loud, Disorder gives its n arches the same weight as the stems, with glyphs kept well apart. Anek Tamil adds big round bowls beneath it, softening the shout.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-anek-telugu: Anek Telugu builds its rhythm from wide bowls that never quite latch shut. Disorder shouts in strokes that never vary in thickness, and the open bowls below it hand the eye somewhere easy to land.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-carrois-gothic-sc: Carrois Gothic SC reads cleanly, each curve ending in a clear opening and its lowercase nearly matching the capitals in height. Text glides along smoothly, while Disorder keeps its single-weight line rough.
